data.name: rDNS
data.description: Allows clients and administrators to create rDNS PTRs from within SynergyCP.
changelog: The IPv6 add field on the Reverse DNS page now shows a generic documentation address (2001:db8::1) as its example.

Fixed the IPv6 tab not appearing on the Reverse DNS page: entity IPv6 assignments are stored in the v6_address field rather than full_ip, so servers with IPv6 on their IP entities did not get the tab. IPv6-only entities no longer break the IPv4 list.
The Reverse DNS page now defaults to 20 rows per page, with a page size selector offering 50, 100, and 500 rows.

The IPv6 tab on the Reverse DNS page now supports adding PTR records for individual IPv6 addresses, validated against the IPv6 ranges assigned to the server, instead of attempting to list every address in a range. The tab is hidden when the server has no IPv6 entities and no existing IPv6 PTR records.
New IPv6 rDNS Limit setting (default 20) caps how many IPv6 PTR records a client can create per IP entity; admins are not limited. Clients get a validation error when the limit is reached.
Package page templates now carry a version marker in their URLs so browser and proxy caches cannot serve stale templates after an upgrade.

The Reverse DNS page now separates IPv4 and IPv6 addresses into tabs (IPv4 selected by default) and paginates both lists at 50 rows per page. The IPv6 tab lists single-address IP entities plus existing IPv6 PTR records, since IPv6 ranges are too large to enumerate row-by-row.

Fixed the new Reverse DNS page and server panel showing raw translation keys (e.g. pkg.rdns.admin.ptr.manage.LINK) when a cached copy of the language file predates 3.0.0: the new labels moved to a new language file that caches have never seen.

Fixed the server page rDNS panel rendering as an empty expanding box with no link after upgrading to 3.0.0: caching proxies could keep serving the pre-3.0 panel template because template URLs are not cache-busted. The template file was renamed so caches are bypassed.

rDNS management has moved from an expanding box on the server page to its own dedicated page in both the admin and client portals, reached via a Manage Reverse DNS button on the server page (URL: /hardware/server/:id/rdns). This prepares the UI for upcoming IPv6 rDNS support, where per-server record lists can be large.
